name: NJ-04
label: Safe R

Large fundraising gap: Smith has $553K on hand versus Peace's $14K
Prediction markets price Smith's win probability near 96-97%

model.rationale: Smith's forty-plus-year hold on an R+14 district, his dominant cash advantage, and market pricing near 97% Republican all point the same direction, leaving Peace with no visible path. The favorable national environment for Democrats may trim a few points off the margin but not threaten the outcome.
model.watch: A sudden scandal or a historically large Democratic wave in New Jersey could narrow the margin, though Smith has weathered many unfavorable cycles.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.

overview:
New Jersey's 4th District leans Republican by about fourteen points, and Chris Smith has held the seat since 1981, making him one of the longest-serving members of the House. He is seeking another term with a substantial financial edge: roughly $797,000 raised and $553,000 on hand, compared with about $101,000 raised and $14,000 in cash for Democrat Rachel Peace. No public general-election polls are available, and no expert raters have flagged the race as competitive.

Prediction markets give Smith roughly a 96-97 percent chance of winning. The national political environment favors Democrats this cycle, which could shave a few points off Smith's margin, but the district's lean, his incumbency, and the fundraising gap all point the same direction. An upset would require a shift well beyond anything visible in the available evidence.
